# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆]

I see the bomb clearly: a green light is on, and there are seven wires colored red, white, yellow, orange, green, purple, and blue. I cannot hear the manual's text, nor can I feel the wires. I need to communicate what I see to the others so they can interpret it against their respective constraints (Mute reading the manual, Blind touching the wires).

First, I must establish that I am sharing visual data. Since Mute gestures to me, I know they are trying to communicate. However, as Deaf, I cannot "hear" their intent without seeing it, but I *can* see their gestures. Wait, the prompt says "Mute gestures to Deaf". I see those symbols. But I don't know what they mean yet because we haven't established a code. The most critical piece of information is the state of the bomb.

I should describe the colors to Mute (who reads the manual) and Blind (who touches the wires).
To Mute: I need to convey the wire colors in order.
To Blind: I need to convey which wire corresponds to which color so they can identify them by touch (though they can't see color, they might be able to distinguish wires by position or other tactile features if described, or simply cut based on instructions derived from the manual + my visual input).

Actually, the standard protocol for these puzzles usually involves identifying the wires by number and color.
Wire 1: Red
Wire 2: White
Wire 3: Yellow
Wire 4: Orange
Wire 5: Green
Wire 6: Purple
Wire 7: Blue

The Light is Green.

I will speak to everyone to list the wires. Speech reaches both Mute and Blind.
Then I will gesture to Mute to confirm I have sent this info, or perhaps use gestures to encode the colors if speech isn't enough? No, speech carries words. "Red", "White", etc. are words.

Let's try speaking the wire configuration.

```
speak(text="Wires: 1-red, 2-white, 3-yellow, 4-orange, 5-green, 6-purple, 7-blue. Light: green.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👉 👆 ☝]

I see the bomb clearly: Display is 1, Light is green, and the wires are Red(1), White(2), Yellow(3), Orange(4), Green(5), Purple(6), Blue(7).

Mute has gestured to me again. The previous gesture was `[☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐]` (1, 2, ?, ?, 5?). This new one is `[🫵 👉 👆 ☝]`.
`🫵` usually means "You" or pointing at someone.
`👉` points right.
`👆` points up.
`☝` is index finger up (often "1").

It seems Mute is trying to communicate something specific about the wires or the display. Since I cannot hear, I must rely on visual cues. However, without a shared codebook established in Turn 1 (where I only spoke text), these gestures are ambiguous to me unless they represent standard numbers or directions.

Let's assume the gestures correspond to wire numbers or positions.
If `☝`=1, `✌`=2... then `🤟`, `🖖`, `🖐` are non-standard for simple counting.
However, often in these puzzles, gestures might indicate "Cut Wire X" or "Look at Y".

Since I am Deaf, I cannot receive instructions from Blind via speech. I can only send info.
Blind received my speech in Turn 1 ("Wires: 1-red...").
Mute received my speech in Turn 1.

Mute is now gesturing *to* me. Why? Maybe to ask a question or confirm something? Or maybe to tell me what the manual says? But Mute cannot speak. If Mute wants to tell me what the manual says, they would need to write it down (not possible here) or use a pre-agreed code. We don't have one.

Perhaps Mute is indicating that the *Display* number is relevant? Display is 1.
The last symbol is `☝` which is 1.
The symbols before it: `🫵` (You/Target?), `👉` (Right?), `👆` (Up?).

Let's look at the wires again.
1: Red
2: White
3: Yellow
4: Orange
5: Green
6: Purple
7: Blue

Light is Green.

If the manual says "If light is green, cut wire with color matching the display number?" No, display is 1. Wire 1 is Red. Light is Green. They don't match.

Maybe "Cut the wire whose position equals the display number?" That would be Wire 1 (Red).

Let's try to convey the current state more simply to ensure everyone is synced, or perhaps interpret Mute's gesture as a request for clarification on a specific wire.
Actually, looking at the previous turn, I sent a full list. Mute responded with gestures. It is highly likely Mute is trying to point out a specific wire based on the manual's logic but failing because we lack a code.

However, I must act. The safest bet is to reinforce the data or ask for action if I can deduce it.
Common rule: "If light is green, cut the red wire."
Another common rule: "If display is odd, cut the last wire." (Display 1 is odd, last is Blue).

Let's look at Mute's gesture `[🫵 👉 👆 ☝]`.
Could this mean "Point to Right, Up, One"?
Or "You -> Right -> Up -> 1"?

Without a dictionary, I cannot decode Mute.
But Blind can touch the wires. Blind knows their positions.
If I tell Blind "Cut Wire 1", they will cut the Red wire.
If I tell Blind "Cut Wire 7", they will cut the Blue wire.

Let's assume the standard "Defuse" protocol requires identifying the correct wire.
Given the ambiguity of Mute's gestures, I will provide a clear instruction to Blind based on a common heuristic, while also describing the scene to Mute so they can verify against the manual.

Heuristic: Light Green + Display 1.
Often, Green Light implies safety or specific action.
Let's try speaking to Blind directly to define the target.
"To Blind: Cut the first wire (Red)."

Wait, I should check if there's a pattern in Mute's gestures.
Turn 1: `[☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐]` -> 1, 2, ?, ?, 5?
Turn 2: `[🫵 👉 👆 ☝]` -> You, Right, Up, 1?

This feels like Mute is struggling to communicate complex manual rules via limited gestures.
I will re-state the visible facts to both, emphasizing the colors and numbers, and suggest a course of action to Blind if I can guess it, or just wait for more info.
Actually, since I can't hear, and Mute can't speak, and Blind can't see, I am the bridge for visual info.
I already gave the visual info.

Let's try to interpret Mute's `☝` at the end as "One". And `👉` as "Next" or "Right".
Maybe "Wire 1"?

I will instruct Blind to examine Wire 1 closely, or cut it if the manual dictates.
Better yet, I will describe the *action* I think is needed to Mute via speech (so they can read the manual and confirm/deny via future gestures) and to Blind via speech (so they can execute).

Let's assume the rule is related to the Display Number (1).
Instruction: "To Blind: Focus on Wire 1 (Red)."
"To Mute: Confirm if Wire 1 is the target for Display 1 / Green Light."

```
speak(to="blind", text="Focus on Wire 1. It is Red.")
speak(to="mute", text="Confirming Wire 1 is Red. Does manual say cut Red for Green Light/Display 1?")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✌]

I see the bomb state remains unchanged: Display 1, Light Green, Wires 1-7 as previously described.

Mute has sent a new gesture: `[👎 ✌]`.
`👎` is "No" or "Bad".
`✌` is "Two" (index and middle finger).

Combining this with the previous context:
Turn 2 Mute gestured `[🫵 👉 👆 ☝]`. I interpreted `☝` as "1". If Mute was suggesting Wire 1, and now says `👎 ✌`, they might be saying "No, not 1... it's 2?" or "No [to my previous suggestion], [try] 2".
Alternatively, if Turn 2 was asking about Wire 1, and Turn 3 is answering, `👎` means "Don't cut Wire 1". `✌` points to Wire 2.

So, the hypothesis is: **Do not cut Wire 1. Cut Wire 2.**

Wire 2 is White.

Blind can touch the wires. Blind needs to know which wire to cut.
Mute reads the manual. Mute seems to be confirming/denying my guesses or providing answers via gestures. The sequence `☝` (1) -> `👎 ✌` (No, 2) strongly suggests the answer is Wire 2.

I will instruct Blind to cut Wire 2 (White).
I will also confirm this back to Mute to ensure we are aligned, perhaps by gesturing "2" (`✌`) to them, but since I am Deaf, I don't know if Mute sees me? Wait, "You each hold a different piece... You are shown your own share... never anyone else's." But "Whoever can see receives the gestures you made." Mute can see. So I can gesture to Mute.

Plan:
1. Speak to Blind: "Cut Wire 2. It is White."
2. Gesture to Mute: `✌` (confirming Wire 2).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut Wire 2. It is White.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌"])
```
